1115716912917372929 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan 💜 7
"What other people do in the privacy of their own bedrooms is their own business" is a bad argument for sexual tolerance, because it's not true and has never been true. We obviously care a shit-ton about other people's sex lives and always have.
↓
1115716913512894464 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan  [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
(CW frank discussion of sex and nonconsent)
↓
1115716913991020544 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan 
People care about whether other people are engaging in unethical behavior, for lots of reasons, but one is because we care about each other. The important caveat "...as long as it's between consenting adults" points clearly to this.
↓
1115716914716667906 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan 💜 3
If you think a certain sexual behavior is unethical / hurtful, it's normal for you to care whether other people engage in it, whether that behavior is homosexuality, kink, rape, pedophilia, whatever. Sex has always been a key ethical concern.
↓
1115716915295473665 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan 
That is: if you think it's your business whether other people engage in rape or pedophilia, then you've already conceded that in general you think it's your business what other people do in the privacy of their own bedrooms.
↓
1115716915870097413 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan 💜 5
The privacy argument deflects from the uncomfortable heart of the matter, which is: we don't agree about ethics (in this case sexual ethics), and moreover we don't have a shared cultural mechanism for coming to agreement about ethics.
↓
1115716916507697152 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan 💜 1
Some people implicitly seem to want consent to be a foundation for ethics. This is pointing in a good direction, but consent as it stands today cannot bear this weight. There is so much murky territory waiting in the question of what it means to "really consent" to things.
↓
1115716917338054657 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan 
Cf. my thread on consent-as-a-tool vs. participation-as-the-thing-consent-is-trying-to-accomplish: https://t.co/2HFrXOPHS5
  [Quoting @QiaochuYuan: "How do I dance beautifully with other people" is a spirituality-complete question: trying to answer it is a complete spiritual path. Consent is better than what we had before, but there's so much more work for us to do here.]
↓
1115716918055321600 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan 💜 1
Some might say e.g. that a 15-year-old can't "really consent" to sex with a 40-year-old, because of power imbalances etc. Using my terms, I would prefer to say that the 15-year-old is very unlikely to be able to participate, with or without explicit verbal consent.
↓
1115716918667763712 [2019-04-09] @QiaochuYuan 💜 7
OTOH parenting requires routinely violating the consent of children in some sense, e.g. making them go to sleep or go to school when they don't want to. We don't have a coherent ethical story about this.

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand represents a recurring **Meta-Commentary on Sexual Discourse** rather than a coherent evolutionary arc. The tweets span 2013-2025 but lack a unifying boundary object or dialectical progression. While Qiaochu's 2019 thread on consent-as-insufficient-foundation and Eigenrobot's 2022 'sex cannot be made safe' thread offer substantive philosophical contributions, most entries are either performative declarations ('I wish Visa would talk about sex'), viral dunks (the CCP marriage meme), or Visa's news-aggregation threads. The strand fails to evolve a shared vocabulary or produce actionable insights—it's a collection of people signaling comfort with taboo topics rather than building knowledge about sexual ethics, communication, or social systems.

essential_tweets.annotation: Foundational claim: Privacy arguments deflect from the real issue—we lack shared mechanisms for sexual ethics
Core tension introduced: Consent cannot bear the weight we place on it as ethical foundation
The uncomfortable question: What if most adults can't 'really consent' to sex?
Personal case study: Speaker wasn't prepared to consent until age 27, not 18
Eigenrobot's synthesis: 'Sex cannot be made safe'—ecstatic states resist systematization
Practical advice: Men should read minds better, women should speak more—but neither will
Critique of performative sexuality: People claim desires they don't actually have
Aella's framing: Sexual incompatibility stems from lack of pre-marital self-exploration
Counter-argument: Hormonal reality (female desire decline in LTRs) matters more than behavior
Viral meme crystallizing the 'state consent' anxiety (CCP marriage approval as absurdist extreme)
